title: Comparative Study of Large Language Models on Chinese Film Script Continuation: An Empirical Analysis Based on GPT-5.2 and Qwen-Max

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating and comparing a US-developed LLM (GPT-5.2) and a Chinese-native LLM (Qwen-Max) on a culturally-specific Chinese film script continuation benchmark. The methodology uses automated metrics (ROUGE-L, Structural Similarity) and LLM-as-Judge scoring to assess the models' ability to understand and generate indigenous cultural elements, linguistic styles, and context-specific narrative paradigms.

Applying Entman's framing theory to conduct a qualitative mechanism attribution analysis of the generated texts, specifically examining the 'Moral Evaluation' dimension to identify shifts in value stances and moral frameworks, which the authors attribute to underlying content moderation mechanisms and alignment training.
